prompt: State what is meant by an elastic collision in the context of the kinetic theory of gases.

mark_scheme.criterion: States that total kinetic energy is conserved (or no loss of kinetic energy during collisions).

hints: Recall what physical quantity is conserved in an elastic collision that is not conserved in an inelastic collision.
solution: An elastic collision is one in which total kinetic energy is conserved (there is no loss of kinetic energy).
teacher_walkthrough: Emphasize the standard Cambridge definition: total kinetic energy is conserved.
Note that momentum is conserved in all collisions, but kinetic energy conservation distinguishes elastic from inelastic collisions.
